#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium,
#                falling back to the first sim_* only when the canonical
#                engine is not built -- see the comment at the default)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own

# `scripts/test_all.sh e2e` works from a fresh shell. An exported value wins;
# the file only supplies what the caller's shell lacks -- same pattern as
# tests/lib. Exported for the child builds (make -C tests/fixtures).
cfg_val() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tail -1; }
for _k in QEMU_BIN_DIR VSIM_BIN_DIR HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN LINUX_TOOLCHAIN; do

    _v="$(cfg_val "$_k")"
    [[ -n "$_v" ]] && export "$_k=$_v"

# require below reports it.

HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Negative test: a corrupted --resume-from-qemu state file must trigger a
# fail-fast in vsim with a recognizable error message, not a segfault, hang,
# or silent forward run on garbage state.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

BAD_STATE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$BAD_STATE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT

# 32 bytes of zeros: shorter than hybrid_state_v1, hits the short-read branch.
dd if=/dev/zero of="$BAD_STATE" bs=32 count=1 status=none

set +e
timeout 10 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$BAD_STATE" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

# 0    - silent pass on garbage (BAD)
# 124  - bash timeout fired -> vsim hung (BAD)
# 200  - hybrid handoff exit (BAD: drain ran, state was treated as valid)
# else - any non-zero error path (OK)
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 124 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: expected non-zero, non-200, non-timeout exit; got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if ! grep -Eq "short read|bad magic|cannot open" "$SIM_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: stderr did not match 'short read|bad magic|cannot open'"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[rt_corrupt_state] PASS: vsim fail-fast with rc=$RC"

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
#   plugin_qemu_drain LOG ARGS [QEMU_ARGS...] - spawn QEMU for a plugin-only
#                               drain test (boots $VSIM_ELF with the plugin
#                               attached); sets RC to QEMU's exit code.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Spawn QEMU for a plugin-only drain test: boot $VSIM_ELF on andes_ae350 with
# the hybrid plugin attached, stdin detached, combined output to LOG.
#   plugin_qemu_drain LOG PLUGIN_ARGS [EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS...]
# PLUGIN_ARGS is the plugin argument string after "$VSIM_PLUGIN," (e.g.
# "outfile=$STATE"). Sets RC to QEMU's exit code -- deliberately not local,
# callers gate on it -- and toggles errexit off around the spawn exactly like
# every call site used to. No shared-memory backend: plugin-only tests have
# no vsim leg, so nothing else ever opens the mmap, and the machine's default
# RAM is the same 128 MiB the backend used to force.
plugin_qemu_drain() {
  local log="$1" plugin_args="$2"; shift 2
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    "$@" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$plugin_args" </dev/null >"$log" 2>&1
  RC=$?
  set -e
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

# looking like coverage while guarding nothing, so a dead row is an error.

BASELINE_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
BASELINE_FILE="${BASELINE_FILE:-$BASELINE_LIB_DIR/../baseline/kernel_cycles.tsv}"

baseline_rows() {
  local f="${1:-$BASELINE_FILE}"
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 1
  awk '!/^[[:space:]]*(#|$)/' "$f"
}

baseline_cycles() {
  local eng="$1" mode="$2" fix="$3" f="${4:-$BASELINE_FILE}"
  [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
  awk -F'\t' -v e="$eng" -v m="$mode" -v x="$fix" \
    '!/^[[:space:]]*(#|$)/ && $1 == e && $2 == m && $3 == x { print $4; exit }' "$f"
}

# KNOWN_FIXTURES is a whitespace-separated list of fixture names the test
# tables actually run; a row outside it can never be checked.
baseline_lint() {
  local known="$1" f="${2:-$BASELINE_FILE}"
  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
    echo "baseline: table not found: $f"
    return 1
  fi
  awk -F'\t' -v known=" $known " '
    BEGIN { rc = 0 }
    function bad(msg) { printf "baseline:%d: %s: %s\n", NR, msg, $0; rc = 1 }
    /^[[:space:]]*(#|$)/ { next }
    {
      if (NF != 4)                       { bad("want 4 tab-separated fields, got " NF); next }
      if ($2 != "marker" && $2 != "pc")  { bad("mode must be marker or pc");            next }
      if ($4 !~ /^[0-9]+$/)              { bad("kernel_cycles must be a decimal count"); next }
      if (index(known, " " $3 " ") == 0) { bad("no test runs fixture " $3);             next }
      key = $1 SUBSEP $2 SUBSEP $3
      if (key in seen)                   { bad("duplicate key, first seen at line " seen[key]); next }
      seen[key] = NR
    }
    END { exit rc }
  ' "$f"
}

cat > scripts/record_baseline.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Record the golden cycle-count baseline (AndeSim S0).
#
# Drives scripts/run_e2e.sh with the gate switched OFF (an empty table), then
# reads the kernel_cycles figure out of the per-test logs that runner already
# writes. There is deliberately no second measuring path: the recorder and
# the checker measure through the SAME harness, so a recorded number is
# reproducible by construction rather than by agreement between two scripts.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/record_baseline.sh                # refresh the rows already there
#   scripts/record_baseline.sh FIXTURE...     # record these fixtures
#
# Env: MODE (marker|pc|both, default both), VSIM_BIN, JOBS -- all passed to
# run_e2e.sh unchanged.
#
# Rows for OTHER engines are kept untouched: you can only measure the engine
# VSIM_BIN points at, so recording one engine must not erase another.
#
# The table is never written unless every requested run produced a number.
# A partial baseline is worse than none -- it looks like coverage.

set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
. "$ROOT/tests/lib/baseline.sh"

TABLE="$BASELINE_FILE"
MODE="${MODE:-both}"

FIXTURES=("$@")
if [ "${#FIXTURES[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # Refresh mode: the table itself names what to measure, so the recorded
  # set can never drift from the enforced set.
  if [ ! -s "$TABLE" ]; then
    echo "record_baseline: $TABLE holds no rows -- name the fixtures to record:" >&2
    echo "  scripts/record_baseline.sh handoff_roundtrip rt_mem_loadstore ..." >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  mapfile -t FIXTURES < <(baseline_rows "$TABLE" | cut -f3 | sort -u)
fi

# run_e2e.sh anchors FILTER as ^...$, so the alternation needs its own group.
FILTER="($(IFS='|'; printf '%s' "${FIXTURES[*]}"))"
EMPTY=$(mktemp)
NEW=$(mktemp)
BODY=$(mktemp)
LOG_DIR=$(mktemp -d -t baseline-XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -f "$EMPTY" "$NEW" "$BODY"' EXIT

echo "==> measuring ${#FIXTURES[@]} fixture(s), mode=$MODE, logs: $LOG_DIR"
BASELINE_FILE="$EMPTY" FILTER="$FILTER" MODE="$MODE" LOG_DIR="$LOG_DIR" \
  bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
RUN_RC=$?

ENGINE=$(cat "$LOG_DIR/engine" 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$ENGINE" ] || { echo "record_baseline: run_e2e.sh named no engine" >&2; exit 1; }

# Harvest. Log names are "<mode>--<test>.log"; the neg drivers measure
# nothing, so only the two trigger modes carry a figure.
missing=0
for log in "$LOG_DIR"/*--*.log; do
  base=$(basename "$log" .log)
  mode="${base%%--*}"
  name="${base#*--}"
  case "$mode" in marker|pc) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  cyc=$(sed -nE 's/.*kernel_cycles\][[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/p' "$log" | head -1)
  if [ -z "$cyc" ]; then
    echo "record_baseline: no cycle count for $name[$mode] -> $log" >&2
    missing=1
    continue
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$ENGINE" "$mode" "$name" "$cyc" >> "$NEW"
done

if [ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 ] || [ "$missing" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$NEW" ]; then
  echo "record_baseline: measurement incomplete (run rc=$RUN_RC) -- $TABLE not touched" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Merge: drop the keys being re-recorded, keep every other row (other
# engines, other fixtures), then append what we just measured.
if [ -s "$TABLE" ]; then
  baseline_rows "$TABLE" | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' '
    NR == FNR { replaced[$1 SUBSEP $2 SUBSEP $3] = 1; next }
    !(($1 SUBSEP $2 SUBSEP $3) in replaced)
  ' "$NEW" - > "$BODY"
fi
cat "$NEW" >> "$BODY"
sort -t$'\t' -k1,1 -k3,3 -k2,2 -o "$BODY" "$BODY"

{
  cat <<'HDR'
# Golden cycle-count baseline -- AndeSim S0.
#
# Each row is the cycle count of one measured region. scripts/run_e2e.sh
# asserts these counts EXACTLY. A move of ONE cycle is a failure, not drift.
#
# Format:   engine <TAB> trigger-mode <TAB> fixture <TAB> kernel_cycles
# Key:      all three of engine, mode and fixture. A cycle count belongs to
#           one engine measuring one region through one trigger mechanism.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The cycle count is what AndeSim sells. The port to FastSim moves guest RAM
# out from under the core, and a change there moves these numbers silently.
# Before the port, nothing caught that: the harness printed the count and
# checked nothing.
#
# THE FIDELITY CONTRACT -- two halves that are easy to confuse
#   * The BYTES of guest RAM MAY move to FastSim's gs_memory. This is allowed.
#   * The response LATENCY that reaches the core MUST NOT change.
# The RTL does not produce that latency. SimpleMemory adds it, in b_transport:
#       delay += sc_core::sc_time(cycles, sc_core::SC_NS);
#   -- vsim_andesim/src/platform/simple_memory.hpp
# Replace SimpleMemory with a model that adds no equivalent delay, and every
# number below moves.
#
# TO CHANGE A NUMBER
# Do not edit a row by hand. Run:
#       scripts/record_baseline.sh [FIXTURE...]
# Then say in the commit message WHY the count moved. A number that moves
# with no reason given is exactly the regression this file exists to catch.
#
HDR
  printf '# Recorded: %s\n#\n' "$(date -I)"
  printf '# engine\tmode\tfixture\tkernel_cycles\n'
  cat "$BODY"
} > "$TABLE"

# Read the table back and confirm it says what we measured -- catches a merge
# or quoting mistake before the file is ever committed.
while IFS=$'\t' read -r e m f c; do
  got=$(baseline_cycles "$e" "$m" "$f" "$TABLE")
  if [ "$got" != "$c" ]; then
    echo "record_baseline: readback mismatch for $f[$m]: wrote $c, read '$got'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done < "$NEW"

echo "==> recorded $(wc -l < "$NEW") row(s) for $ENGINE into $TABLE"
SH
chmod +x scripts/record_baseline.sh
bash -n scripts/record_baseline.sh && bash -n scripts/run_e2e.sh && echo "syntax ok"

cat > /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/drivers/baseline_table_wired.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Negative test: scripts/run_e2e.sh really hands the baseline table to the
# gate inside tests/e2e.sh.
#
# tests/drivers/baseline_cycle_mismatch.sh proves the GATE bites. This proves
# the WIRING between them. A runner that read the table and then forgot to
# pass the value through would leave every row passing vacuously -- from the
# outside, identical to having no baseline at all.
#
# Method: take the fixture's COMMITTED count, offset it by one cycle in a
# throwaway table, and require the sweep to fail over that one cycle. The
# offset is applied to every engine's row for the fixture, so this driver
# needs no opinion about which engine is installed.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/baseline.sh"

NAME=baseline_table_wired
FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
MODE=marker

BAD=$(mktemp); trap 'rm -f "$BAD"' EXIT
baseline_rows | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' -v f="$FIXTURE" -v m="$MODE" \
  '$3 == f && $2 == m { $4 = $4 + 1; print }' > "$BAD"
[ -s "$BAD" ] \
  || fail "$NAME: the committed table has no $FIXTURE[$MODE] row to offset"

OUT=$(BASELINE_FILE="$BAD" FILTER="$FIXTURE" MODE="$MODE" \
      bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh" 2>&1)
RC=$?

# An unbuilt simulator also exits non-zero; that is a skip, not a pass.
if printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'build artifacts first'; then
  echo "[skip] $NAME: simulator not built"
  exit 77
fi

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "$OUT"
  fail "$NAME: the sweep passed against a baseline offset by one cycle"
fi
if ! printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq 'kernel_cycles [0-9]+ != baseline [0-9]+'; then
  echo "$OUT"
  fail "$NAME: failed (rc=$RC), but not over the baseline comparison"
fi

ok "$NAME: the runner feeds the table to the gate (rc=$RC)"
SH
chmod +x /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/drivers/baseline_table_wired.sh
cd /home/nick/work/andesim && bash tests/drivers/baseline_table_wired.sh; echo "--- rc=$? ---"
